constraints.text: Exact pricing algorithms for commodity market dynamics
Specific combat balance and enemy AI behavior parameters
Precise visual effects implementation details (particle systems, shaders)
Optimal canvas/WebGL rendering approach for the target hardware
Exact save/load format and storage mechanism (localStorage vs files)
the delivered product is synthesized and assembled as one whole that is runnable locally
an ordered smoke test performs the install step, then the start step, then reaches the running product

assumptions: Node.js is available on the development machine
Chrome is the target browser and will be used for testing
The player has basic familiarity with space trading games
A 2020 laptop is a reasonable minimum hardware target for 60fps
WebSocket or similar real-time communication is not required (single-player)
Local filesystem access for save/load is acceptable
payload.candidate_scope: The minimum useful product scope includes: a Node.js server that serves a single HTML/JS frontend; a canvas/WebGL rendering system with parallax starfield; at least 8 named star systems with stations; a commodity market with dynamic per-system pricing; hyperspace jump mechanics with fuel consumption and pirate encounter probability; ship-to-ship combat with player lasers vs enemy AI; ship upgrades (cargo capacity, laser, shields, fuel tank); save/load game state functionality; unit tests for core mechanics; a browser smoke test; and a /healthz endpoint on the server.

The system will consist of a Node.js backend serving a single-page canvas/WebGL frontend with parallax starfield, hyperspace jump effects, station docking screens, ship HUD, commodity market with dynamic pricing, and arcade laser combat.
payload.problem_statement: The initiative aims to create a single-player space trading and combat game inspired by the classic Elite. The problem being addressed is the need for an engaging browser-based game that combines economic trading mechanics with arcade-style combat, running entirely locally without external dependencies.
payload.rationale: The initiative is well-scoped for an XS complexity web-app with clear functional and non-functional requirements. The gameplay mechanics are classic and well-understood, reducing design uncertainty. The technical stack (Node.js + canvas/WebGL) is mature and capable of delivering the required experience. The constraints are reasonable and aligned with the complexity rating. No blockers or fundamental feasibility concerns were identified.

Technical risk: Ensuring no external CDN dependencies while maintaining visual quality
